newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/INDEX VOLATILITIES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/INDEX VOLATILITIES MIXED.

text.p: Implied volatilities in major U.S. stock indexes were mixed Friday amid the market's weakness linked to a sell-off in bonds, traders said.
Volatilities in S&P 500 .SPX and S&P 100 .OEX options were slightly firmer, but were down in S&P 500 futures options.

"Volatility's up a little bit, but it's really gone nowhere," said one SPX trader, who added that the biggest trade was a sale of the December 995 calls. The SPX December 995 call traded about 2,325 contracts by late morning and was down 3-1/2 at 32. Open interest through Thursday was 12,413.
The spot SPX index was down 10.41 at 943.88, off its 939.70 session low reached as bonds dropped sharply on a stronger-than-expected July National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM).
September S&P 500 futures sank 13.95 to 944. Earlier they fell their initial 15-point down limit, reaching 942.95.
"Once bonds came back we came off our lock-down limit," said one S&P 500 futures-options trader. "We haven't tested that low again.
"We're watching bonds basically."
He said volatilities in the August and September contracts were down slightly, with August volatility slipping to around 20 percent, down about half a percentage point.
Volatility in the September series was about 20.8 percent.
"September is relatively firm," the trader said.
In the OEX, volatility as measured by the volatility index .VIX, which is calculated off certain front-month options, was up 1.10, or 4.65 percent, at 24.85. It reached a session high of 25.08.
Traders said activity had quieted after the early flurry of activity, but some expected a pickup in the afternoon.
The S&P 500 futures-options trader said volatilities may ease a bit more later in the session as dealers factor in weekend time decay.
He said the market may remain weak but some buying could emerge, particularly if bonds recover some lost ground.
"The day's move has already been made and now the question is do they test the lows," he said.
He added that a move in the September S&P 500 futures back above 950 could trigger additional buying.
Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said he still expected the market to rally.
He explained that the market fell "on an air pocket" that was mainly a function of poor liquidity rather than a steady decline and that the session low was in place early.

"Bull markets have a tendency to be weak early in the day and strong late in the day," he said in an intraday report. He added, however, that a break of the September S&P 500 futures morning low at 942.95 would be a sign of weakness.
Hegarty added that first-of-the-month buying should help boost the market later in the session.
